title: Making -s scripts load before --options dump
answers: Why are script options missing from --options dump?
How to make scripts load before options dump at startup
Where is the first load of a Script deferred?
body:
`Script.__init__(path, reload=True)` (addons/script.py) does NOT load synchronously: it starts `Script.watcher()` as an asyncio task, and the first `loadscript` happens after an `asyncio.sleep(0)`. Only reload=False loads immediately in `__init__`.
In `tools/main.py:run.main()` the `--options` dump happens before `master.run()`, so script-defined options aren't registered yet.
Fix pattern used: `Script.first_load = asyncio.Event()` set after first load attempt (also if file vanishes), `ScriptLoader.wait_for_scripts()` awaits all of them, and `main()` awaits `master.addons.get("scriptloader").wait_for_scripts()` on the --options path before `dump_defaults`. `AddonManager.get(name)` (addonmanager.py) looks up by addon name.
`main.run` is `# pragma: no cover`, so no direct unit test hook.
applies: Only for scripts loaded with reload=True via ScriptLoader.configure; needs an event loop running (inside main()).
invalidReason: The fix pattern described in the note does not exist in the current code. The note claims Script.first_load, ScriptLoader class, and wait_for_scripts() method were implemented, but none of these appear in the codebase. The main() function in tools/main.py has no await call for script loading before dump_defaults. The fundamental async loading problem still exists but the proposed fix was never implemented.
